info.title: Modat Magnify API
info.description:
Introducing the Modat Magnify API. This powerful tool is designed for proactive cybersecurity efforts. It allows you
to search, analyse, and retrieve detailed information about internet-connected IP infrastructure and DNS records.
For the data model, the query language, and worked examples, see the
[Modat Resource Center](https://magnify.modat.io/docs).

Please note, API access follows [Modat’s Terms of Service](https://magnify.modat.io/terms-of-service).
We kindly ask that all automated interactions go through this API.

### Authentication

All API endpoints require authentication using an API key that should be included in the `Authorization` header of each
request. Prefixing the API key with `Bearer <api_key>` is optional.

### Rate Limiting

Search and data-retrieval endpoints enforce rate limiting based on your subscription level. Management endpoints use a
separate bucket with a higher limit of 10 requests per second for
lightweight requests such as quota usage, query history and bulk export. The API uses a sliding time window of
3 seconds to calculate your request rate. If you exceed your allowed request rate,
requests are rejected with HTTP 429. Rate-limit responses include a `Retry-After` header containing the number of seconds
to wait before retrying. For optimal performance, distribute your requests evenly rather than sending them in bursts.

### Deprecation Policy

When a field or endpoint is scheduled for removal, it is first marked as deprecated in this OpenAPI specification
(`deprecated: true`) and remains fully functional for a transition period of at least one month. After that period it
may be removed without further notice. If you generate client code from this specification, regenerate it periodically
and migrate away from deprecated fields as soon as they appear.

### Usage Guidelines

Please refer to the endpoint documentation below for specific request and response formats.

fields.title: Fields
fields.description: Dotted paths of the fields to export, matched with fnmatch (e.g. `service.tls.*`). `service` and `services` are aliases at both search levels. Null exports all fields.

FacetBucket.title: FacetBucket
FacetBucket.description: One term-facet bucket as returned by the faceted search endpoints.

ScannedServiceModel.title: ScannedServiceModel
ScannedServiceModel.description:
One service exactly as a single scan saw it, with nothing enriched around it.

The enriched view (`ServiceQueryModel`) adds what the ingest pipeline derives per host —
fqdns, asn, geo, fingerprints, CVEs — none of which a scan produces. Served on its own
wherever the answer must be one scan and not the current state of the service: a point in
the service's history, or the outcome of a live scan.

SearchLevel.title: SearchLevel
SearchLevel.description: The level that the search query is executed at.
